messages:
Maya (CSM): quick check — BlueHarbor (onboarding) had a third repeat 503 cluster this week. Usage is up (+38% q/q) but latency and error rate spiking during their batch imports. Sending this thread to capture owners + action items.

Jamal (Support): seeing the same. Root looks like upstream timeout on model shard A when seq_len > 2048. Spike aligns with their nightly bulk ingest window. Ticket created: CS-8943.

Ravi (Solutions Eng): rough query I ran:
```
index=prod-logs service=inference host=rt-* status=503 "shard=A" | stats count by time(1h), request_seq_len | sort -time
```
shows the rate jumps from ~2/hr to ~60/hr between 02:00-03:00 UTC.

Maya (CSM): thanks. BlueHarbor is on a renewal review next month; we need a mitigation plan and timeline. Anya, can you lead customer comms once we have the fix path? :pray:

Anya (AM): yes. I'll message Evelyn and set expectation: probable short-term mitigation + longer-term config change.

Jamal (Support): provisional mitigations I can push:
- throttle concurrent batch jobs for that customer (rate limiter)
- fall back to model-compat variant (quantized) for large seqs
- temporary increased retry/backoff to avoid thundering
I'll test rate limiter policy in staging and report.

Ravi (Solutions Eng): long-term fix ideas:
- kernel-level patch to avoid OOM on shard A for >2048 tokens (requires runtime release)
- smarter routing: route BlueHarbor's nightly to dedicated pool at lower concurrency
Estimated ETA: routing change = 2 business days, runtime patch = 3-4 weeks (CI + canary).

Maya (CSM): great. Let's capture owners + deadlines here so I can update the renewal playbook.

Jamal (Support): I own immediate throttle test. ETA: EOD tomorrow (1768590721).

Ravi (Solutions Eng): I'll scope routing change and open infra PR. ETA: draft by tomorrow afternoon, canaries next day.

Anya (AM): I'll draft customer note after Jamal confirms throttle outcome. ETA: T+1 after confirmation.

Maya (CSM): action items summary (for playbook):
- Jamal: implement & validate throttle policy in staging; roll to prod if green (owner).
- Ravi: implement routing to dedicated pool as interim; open PR + run canary (owner).
- Ravi: schedule runtime kernel patch planning w/ eng-runtime (long-term).
- Anya: customer comms & renewal note.
- Maya: update renewal risk tracker and escalate to RevOps if spend deviation persists.

deploy-bot: Deployment recorded: infra-routing-change branch created by ravi at 1768507820.

Jamal (Support): small update — throttle test in staging reduced 503s by ~85% during synthetic night window. Logs attached.

Maya (CSM): excellent. Can we get prod rollout target?

Ravi (Solutions Eng): aiming to route their nightly to dedicated pool tonight at 03:30 UTC as a canary low-risk window. I'll watch metrics.

Maya (CSM): perfect — I'll set a joint check-in 04:15 UTC to confirm. Anya, I'll hold off on external comms until we confirm canary success.

Anya (AM): acknowledged. I'll prepare an FAQ for the customer (short technical summary + expected timeline).

Jamal (Support): follow-up note: ticket CS-8943 updated with staging test artifacts and suggested prod throttle policy: `policy: customer_id=BH, max_concurrent_batches=4, burst=2`.

Maya (CSM): closing loop — owners and next steps captured. I'll update the weekly account health doc and the renewal risk board. If the canary fails, we'll escalate to SRE and consider temporary credit.

Ravi (Solutions Eng): will post canary status here after 04:20 UTC.

Maya (CSM): thanks team. :thumbsup:
